sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
The path was not smooth: revenue fell 6.8% in FY2020 and was flat at 0.2% growth in FY2023 [D130][D284].
FY2023's stall came with a 21.6pp operating-margin drop, driven by $2.17 billion of inventory provisions for excess Ampere Gaming and Data Center supply [D299][P35][P38].
The FY2024-FY2026 surge was driven by data center compute and networking for accelerated computing and AI, with Blackwell the majority of Data Center revenue in FY2026 [P10][P16].
Data Center grew from 19.9% of revenue in FY2018 to 89.7% in FY2026 [D598][D620].
In FY2026 Data Center contributed 60.2pp of the 65.5% revenue growth, with Networking alone adding 14.1pp [D622][D448][D636].
The filing attributes the FY2026 move to Data Center computing up 59% on Blackwell demand and networking up 142% on NVLink and Ethernet/InfiniBand [P8].
Operating income grew 60.1% against 65.5% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 57.3% [D449][D448][D475].
Diluted EPS rose 66.7% against 64.7% net income growth as the diluted share count fell 1.2% [D452][D450][D470].
Operating margin of 60.4% in FY2026 sits well above the 32.8% window median but below the 62.4% FY2025 high [F50][D813][D812].
The FY2026 margin fell 2.0pp, with cost of revenue subtracting 3.9pp, partly offset by R&D and SG&A adding 1.3pp and 0.6pp [D463][D477][D478][D479].
Operating expenses rose 41% on compensation, employee growth and compute and infrastructure costs [P9].
The FY2023 low of 15.7% reflected the $2.17 billion inventory charge, which cut gross margin to 56.9% [F47][D811][P35].
Net margin held at 55.6% despite the operating decline, helped by $11.1 billion of other income from unrealized investment gains including Intel stock [F70][X120][P3].
Operating cash flow of $102.7 billion was 0.86x net income in FY2026, the window low [F100][F60][D435].
Free cash flow of $96.7 billion was a 44.8% margin, against a 44.4% window median [F110][D432][D822].
Capex of $6.04 billion was 2.8% of revenue and 2.13x D&A, up from 0.71x in FY2024 [F105][D431][D437][D327].
Receivables grew 66.8% and inventory 112.3%, both faster than revenue, holding DSO at 65 days and lifting inventory days to 125 [D473][D474][D445][D446].
Net cash fell to $2.14 billion, just 1.0% of revenue, from $34.7 billion a year earlier [D441][D442][D386].
The drop came from $52.2 billion of investing outflow, driven by higher equity securities purchases and the Groq license agreement [F120][P1].
Net cash still ranks at the 83rd percentile of six semis peers, whose median is -13.9% of revenue [D844][D845].
Buybacks and dividends of $41.1 billion absorbed 42.5% of free cash flow, and the current ratio of 3.91x sits below the 4.61x median [D443][D444][F190][D831].
Graphics was 44.1% of revenue and fell 25.0% in FY2023, the one flagged candidate [R1][D753][D754].
That episode looks cyclical rather than structural, since Graphics revenue recovered to $22.5 billion in FY2026 [S125].
Customer concentration is high: one direct customer was 22% of FY2026 revenue and another 14% [P6].
Product revenue members sum to 190% of consolidated revenue in FY2026, so segment shares must not be added [R2].
Operating margin: a print below the 62.4% FY2025 high would extend the FY2026 compression, visible in the next 10-K [D812].
Cash conversion: operating cash flow below 0.86x net income would mark a new window low [D435].
Net cash: a further fall below the $2.14 billion FY2026 level would erode the balance-sheet cushion [D441].
